concepts.learning_objective: Explain why nationalism is a powerful but hard-to-define political creed.
Identify how nationalism led both to unification of states and to the break-up of empires.
Distinguish unifying nationalism from separatist nationalist movements within existing states.

topics.title: Nation: shared beliefs, history and territory

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how a nation differs from a family or kinship group and why it is called an imagined community.
Describe how shared beliefs and a continuing historical identity constitute a nation.
Explain the significance of territory and homeland, and why it causes conflict.

topics.title: Shared political ideals and common political identity

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why a shared vision of the future and political values distinguish nations from other groups.
Evaluate why democracies should imagine the nation in political rather than cultural terms.
State the meaning of the right to national self-determination and its use by liberation movements.
Analyse the consequences of reorganising boundaries on the principle of one culture-one state.
Interpret the Basque demand for self-determination and the democratic alternative to new states.
Identify group rights given to minorities and the reinterpretation of self-determination.
Explain Rabindranath Tagore's critique of narrow nationalism.
Evaluate why an inclusive citizenship that accommodates many identities is needed in a democracy.
